criterion: Each is pinned by a named test and a mutation-audit entry, and the claims about what the existing tests guard are corrected where they were too strong
summary: Count verified three ways: len(GUARDS) 45 with 45 unique names, 45 Guard( openers and 45 pinned_by lines in the text, and the audit's own summary. Both audits quoted verbatim, 8 of 8 and 45 of 45 pinned with nothing uncovered or miscredited. The reviewer did not accept the corrected comments on reading, having noted the executor was previously wrong in both directions about its own tests. For the pipe test it verified both halves: reverting the whole block to the read_text that shipped fails it with subprocess.TimeoutExpired in 60.087s, matching the claimed 60.18s, while the audit's one-line mutation lets it pass in 0.111s - so 'not idle' and 'cannot separate this line from a non-blocking open' are both true. For the never-written case it confirmed graphctl init creates the journal before doctor reads it, that the doctor-level test passes under the mutation, and - checking the other direction too - that injecting an OSError in place of scandir makes it fail, so it is a live false-positive guard rather than dead weight. It applied the FileNotFoundError-to-_NeverRaised mutation by hand after proving the copy is what gets imported, and the named test failed as declared. Gates: 429 tests OK on both interpreters, black, mypy, sync_adapters and graphctl validate all clean.
